questions.q: Why did David want to show kindness to Hanun after Hanun’s father Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, died?
questions.a: David wanted to show kindness to Hanun because Hanun’s father had been kind to David.

questions.q: What did the leaders of Ammon think David’s men were actually trying to do when they entered their land?
questions.a: The leaders thought David’s men were coming to explore and spy on the land so David could conquer it.

questions.q: What did Hanun do to David’s servants that made them deeply ashamed?
questions.a: Hanun shaved off their beards and cut off the lower part of their robes so that their buttocks were exposed.

questions.q: Why did the Ammonites hire chariots and horsemen from the Arameans?
questions.a: They hired the chariots and horsemen to prepare for war because they realized they had greatly insulted David.

questions.q: Who did David send when he heard about the Ammonites preparing for war?
questions.a: David sent Joab and his entire army.

questions.q: Where did the Ammonite soldiers position themselves for battle?
questions.a: The Ammonite soldiers formed a battle line at the entrance of their city, while the kings who had come to help them positioned their armies in the open fields.

questions.q: How did Joab arrange for fighting the Ammonites and the Arameans when he saw their battle lines?
questions.a: Joab chose some of Israel’s best soldiers to fight the Arameans and gave the rest of the army to his brother Abishai to fight the Ammonites.

questions.q: What did Joab tell his brother?
questions.a: Joab told his brother that they should help each other, if needed, and that they should be strong because Yahweh will do what is good for his people.

questions.q: Why did the army of Ammon flee back to their city?
questions.a: The army of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled before the army of Israel, and so they ran back to their city.

questions.q: Why did David gather all Israel together and arrange for battle against the Arameans?
questions.a: David heard that the Arameans had sent for reinforcements.

questions.q: Why were the people of Aram no longer willing to help the Ammonites?
questions.a: They no longer helped the Ammonites after David defeated them in battle and killed their commander.

commentary.text: —The history is here repeated which we read 2Sa 10. The only safety of sinners consists in submitting to the Lord, seeking peace with him, and becoming his servants. Let us assist each other in a good cause; but let us fear lest, while made instruments of good to others, we should come short of salvation, through unbelief and sin.
